input: Get a quote for a custom fence along the driveway

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The total length of the driveway directly determines materials and labor cost, and affects how many contractors need to be contacted.
The fence material (wood, vinyl, metal, chain-link, etc.) drastically changes cost, aesthetics, and which specialists to contact.
Knowing whether this is for a private home, rental property, or HOA-governed community affects who must approve the project and who is involved in decisions.
A budget ceiling determines whether to get one quote or several, and whether premium materials are worth exploring.
Local permit requirements, HOA rules, or utility lines near the driveway could add steps before any contractor visit is meaningful.
Whether the user wants one quote or multiple competitive quotes, and whether they prefer in-person visits or online estimates, shapes the immediate action.
Understanding what 'done well' means — lowest price, fastest install, best warranty, or a specific look — determines how to evaluate and compare quotes.

gold.taskTitle: Get a custom driveway fence quote
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to obtain a price quote for installing a custom fence along their driveway.

questions.title: How long is the driveway section to be fenced?
questions.description: Establish the approximate linear footage of fence needed, as this is the primary driver of material and labor costs.

questions.title: What material do you have in mind for the fence?
questions.description: Identify the preferred fence material (e.g., wood, vinyl, wrought iron, aluminum, chain-link) to target the right contractors and pricing.

questions.title: Is this property subject to HOA or local permit rules?
questions.description: Determine whether approvals, permits, or design restrictions must be accounted for before requesting contractor quotes.

questions.title: Who else is involved in approving this decision?
questions.description: Clarify if a partner, landlord, property manager, or other stakeholder needs to be part of the process.

questions.title: Do you have a budget ceiling for this project?
questions.description: A budget limit helps narrow the scope of quotes and determines whether to pursue premium or standard options.

questions.title: How many quotes do you want, and from what type of source?
questions.description: Establish whether the user wants a single trusted contractor, three competitive bids, or online estimate tools — this defines the immediate next action.

questions.title: What matters most when comparing the quotes you receive?
questions.description: Identify the user's top priority — lowest price, fastest timeline, best warranty, specific aesthetic — so quotes can be evaluated meaningfully.
